text:
toni: Heads-up: customer hit runtime errors on Edge because our ESM entry still imports a transitive `node:crypto` shim. They import the package directly in an Edge route and it throws.

adrian: Noted. We currently map `import` -> dist/esm/index.mjs which contains some node-shim imports from an old helper.

mei: Quick options: (1) Feature-detect and polyfill at runtime (yuck), (2) Produce a small `edge.mjs` ESM build with no node deps and add an `edge` condition to `exports`, (3) expose `./edge` subpath so consumers can import explicitly. I prefer (2)+(3).

toni: Agreed. If we add an `exports` entry like:

```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "edge": "dist/esm/edge.mjs",
    "import": "dist/esm/node.mjs",
    "require": "dist/cjs/index.js",
    "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts"
  },
  "./edge": {
    "import": "dist/esm/edge.mjs",
    "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts"
  }
}
```

mei: For TypeScript we must keep `types` top-level for some packagers, and also include the `exports.".".types` so node12-style resolution can find it. Also add `typesVersions` if we need backward compatibility.

adrian: CI: we'll publish a canary and run two smoke tests: node quickstart (CJS path) and an Edge fixture (Vercel/Cloudflare) that imports the package and performs an auth flow. Fail if `ReferenceError: crypto` or `Buffer is not defined` occur.

toni: Also let's stop publishing `module` top-level; rely on `exports`. But keep `module` for one release as deprecated to avoid breaking older rollups. Add a changelog note.

pkg-bot: canary published -> redwood-sdk@0.0.0-canary-1732104567; ci jobs queued -> canary-edge-smoke/1732104567

mei: I'll add a tiny `lib/edge-adapter.ts` to normalize fetch/Response shapes so retry code can call `headers.get` safely across runtimes. We should also run `tsc --noEmit` and `tsd` against the tarball types.

adrian: I'll draft the PR with export map, edge build, types mapping, canary CI. Ping UX/docs to add a quick note about `import from 'redwood-sdk/edge'` in Edge quickstarts.

toni: Thanks — this should cut down on support tickets and make ESM/Edge DX much better.
